verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents per-task concurrency caps through the queue's `concurrencyLimit` and per-user/per-tenant queueing through concurrency keys, which covers the core 'one hot customer can't starve the rest' need. The evidence shows no user-configurable rate limiting per workflow, key, or tenant; the Limits page only shows the platform's own rate-limit usage. missing for 10: configurable per-workflow/per-key/per-tenant rate limits, in-depth docs on concurrency-key fairness behavior, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I cap concurrency and set rate limits per workflow, per key, or per tenant so one hot customer can't starve the rest

citations.quote: You can set the concurrency limit for a task by setting the `concurrencyLimit` property on the task's queue. This limits the number of runs that can be executing at any one time
With concurrency keys you can create bespoke queue logic for each of your users.
